text:
eli: FYI customer sent an alert — large spike in streaming bill during a regional route-swap. looks like some sessions were double-counted during handoff. anyone seen this pattern before? :confused:

rachel: seen similar but not with this magnitude. do we have routing logs for the time range? share trace id and a session id if possible.

eli: trace=tr_2026_03_swap_14; sess=s-a4c2ff. quick log excerpt attached: 
```
2026-03-24T03:41:02Z INFO shard=us-e1 route_claim session=s-a4c2ff lease=ln-42 owner=pool-us-e1
2026-03-24T03:41:03Z INFO drain_initiate shard=us-e1 target=pool-us-e2 session=s-a4c2ff
2026-03-24T03:41:03Z INFO resume_request shard=us-e2 session=s-a4c2ff resume_token=rt_1
2026-03-24T03:41:03Z INFO billing_mark session=s-a4c2ff lease=ln-42 status=active
2026-03-24T03:41:04Z INFO resume_handled shard=us-e2 session=s-a4c2ff lease=ln-43 billing_mark=active
2026-03-24T03:41:05Z INFO lease_tombstone lease=ln-42
```
Observation: resume_handled came before tombstone; billing pipeline treats resume_handled as start -> both ln-42 and ln-43 counted.

devon: that's the race we've feared. two options I can think of quickly: a) require resume requests to carry previous lease id via X-Prev-Lease header so the server can emit a single lifecycle event referencing both leases; b) keep resume token as-is but change billing to treat resume_handled as start only if no previous active lease seen in last N seconds. both have tradeoffs.

rachel: product/ops note: customers only see a token cost bump and no visibility which route caused it. we should add a per-tenant "handshake anomalies" timeseries in the console so SRE and customers can correlate spikes with route swaps. low-effort first step.

eli: agree. short-term plan: add console metric + an alert threshold, increase sample collection around route-swap windows. long-term: choose an API change. prefer minimal client impact.

devon: technically the header is easiest for rollouts (server ignores unknown headers), but many SDKs are language-bound and we'd need docs updates. Encoding prev-lease into resume_token is backwards-compatible from the server side but requires token re-issuance for tokens that don't include that field.

ops-bot: note: canary proposal created -> us-e2 streaming-service v2026.03.24-canary. Will run for 30m.

rachel: design question for the billing folks: if we add prev-lease to resume, how should billing dedupe work? match on session_id+lease_range?

billing-bot: suggestion: emit a canonical lifecycle event when resume handled that includes: session_id, prev_lease_id (optional), new_lease_id, event_time, event_type. Billing dedupe rule: if a resume event references a prev_lease issued within last 60s, consider the prev_lease as continued rather than new-start. Reconcile offline with lease_tombstone events.

eli: that lifecycle event is the nicest for consumers. console and billing can both look at it. downside: requires changes in several places: resume handler, token parsing, event bus schema.

devon: quick implementation sketch: add optional "prev_lease" field to resume_token.v2 JSON payload (base64), bump token version. Server-side: if token.version==2 parse prev_lease, emit lifecycle event {start->resume with prev_lease}. clients with v1 tokens unaffected. rollout: issue new tokens on login/refresh path; for long-lived tokens fall back to header approach for older clients.

rachel: timeline ask: can we get console metric + alert in next 48h? customers are already opening tickets.

devon: I can wire a temporary console alert that looks for active_count delta > 2.5x over 5m and emits a tenant-level "possible-handshake-dup" flag. will push today.

eli: thanks. assign followups: DEV-987 (token v2 spec) -> devon; CORE-2401 (lifecycle event schema) -> billing team; OPS-941 (console alert + sampling bump) -> rachel.

rachel: I'll post the console PR link once created. also adding a short blurb in the status page to pre-empt customer confusion.

eli: perfect. let's track in the incident channel as well if more customers pop up. :thumbsup:
